## Shared infrastructure — `@keenmate/web-components-devkit` (read before touching examples/build files)

This repo follows the Keenmate component standard: the BlissFramework rulebook
(`C:\Git\BlissFramework\guidelines\web-components\` — structure, naming, CSS,
theming, README, CEM, publish) plus the devkit (`../web-components`, published
as `@keenmate/web-components-devkit`), which owns the example-site kit, the
Vite/Playwright configs and the deploy files. Do not re-create or patch those
locally — every local fork is how they drifted apart.

- **Never add** `examples-chapter-nav.js`, `examples-copy-link.js`,
  `examples-controls-store.js`, `examples-shared.css`, `plausible-snippet.html`
  or `scripts/check-variable-manifest.mjs`. The chapter nav, copy-link buttons,
  shared styles, theme switch, version badge and analytics are injected into
  every root `*.html` page by the Vite plugin automatically.
- **Generated — do not edit:** `Dockerfile`, `nginx.conf`, `Makefile`,
  `.dockerignore` (they start with a `GENERATED by kmwc sync` header). Change
  `package.json#kmwc` and run `npx kmwc sync`, or fix the template in the devkit.
  Repo-specific make targets go in `Makefile.local`.
- **Per-component settings** (title, tagline, CSS prefix, ports, accent colours,
  analytics id, image name, canonical origin) live **only** in `package.json#kmwc`.
- **Example page styles:** shared rules are in `@layer kmwc` and read
  `--base-*` tokens (pages support light / dark / auto via the theme switch), so
  any unlayered rule wins. Put component-only rules in `examples-local.css`.
  Re-theme with `kmwc.theme.accentColor`, never by copying CSS. Native form
  controls (inputs, selects, checkboxes, radios, `role="switch"`, buttons) and
  tables are already styled by the kit (`.reference-table`, `.table-striped`,
  `.table-compact`, …) — don't restyle them per page; `kmwc-native` opts an
  element out. Log lines take the kit tones (`.log-line--ok|info|warn|err|muted`,
  `--action`, timeline cells `.log-line__time` …) — don't colour them per page;
  write event-log lines with `appendLogLine(panel, { name, detail, variant })`
  from `@keenmate/web-components-devkit/examples`, never an `innerHTML` template.
  `<kbd>`, `<mark>`, field widths (`.w-xs` … `.w-lg`) and `.push-end` are kit
  too — no inline styles for them. Page colours come from the kit's `--kmwc-*`
  tokens or `light-dark()` — a literal doesn't follow dark mode (doctor warns);
  a demo that shows fixed colours on purpose goes in `<style data-kmwc-fixed-colors>`
  (one rule: a `/* kmwc-fixed-colors: why */` comment before it; an element's own
  `style="…"`: the attribute on the element).
  If a second component needs a pattern, it belongs in the devkit.
- **Example pages are fragments:** no `<html>`/`<head>`/`<header>` — start with
  `<meta name="kmwc:title" content="…">`, the devkit layout adds the rest. Shared text
  goes in `partials/` via `<kmwc-include>`; show code with `<kmwc-demo>` (the live
  markup IS the snippet) — never hand-copy a demo into a `.code-block`.
- **Every example has a permanent code:** each `<h2>` starts `TH07 · Title`
  (page prefix + number; a plain `Summary` is exempt). New examples take the
  next free number; never renumber or reuse one — the rules are the rulebook's
  `example-pages.md`.
- **Controls persistence:**
  `import { attachControlsPersistence } from '@keenmate/web-components-devkit/examples'`.
  **Landing page:** `renderExamplesIndex({ pages })` from the same module.
- **Found a bug in a shared helper?** Fix it in `../web-components` (so every
  component gets it), not here. Say so in your summary if you can't.
- **Never ship AI-assistant files:** `package.json` `files` must keep
  `"!**/CLAUDE.md"` and `"!**/.claude"` (a `CLAUDE.md` you add under `src/` is
  otherwise published with it).
- Before finishing: `npx kmwc doctor` must pass — it runs the devkit checks,
  checks the `npm pack` file list for dev-only files, and runs the rulebook's
  `*.checks.sh` suites. A rulebook failure that is a real architectural decision
  goes into `VALIDATION-NOTES.md` under a `## C-XX-N — …` heading (deferrals
  don't count). After changing a page, `npx kmwc check-pages` loads every page at
  desktop and phone widths and reports errors, horizontal overflow and page CSS
  that only matches inside a shadow root (markup a render callback draws there is
  out of page CSS's reach — style it through the component's styles hook).

## Project Structure (Monorepo)

This is an npm workspaces monorepo with the following structure:

```
web-grid/
├── package.json              # Workspace root
├── packages/
│   └── web-grid/             # Library package (@keenmate/web-grid)
│       ├── package.json
│       ├── tsconfig.json
│       ├── vite.config.ts
│       └── src/
│           ├── grid.ts       # Core GridEngine class (state, logic)
│           ├── web-component.ts  # GridElement (DOM, events, rendering)
│           ├── types.ts      # All TypeScript type definitions
│           ├── interaction.ts # GridController, callback contexts, action items, event map
│           ├── controller.ts # el.controller facade (createGridController)
│           ├── index.ts      # Main entry point
│           ├── css/          # Modular CSS files
│           └── modules/      # Feature modules
├── index.html, examples-*.html  # Examples site (devkit fragment pages, root vite.config.ts)
├── test/                     # e2e fixture pages (test/*.html) — e2e/ specs target these, never examples
├── e2e/                      # Playwright specs (devkit preset, playwright.config.ts)
├── docs/                     # Internal design notes (action-pipeline.md, z-index-layers.md)
├── Makefile                  # GENERATED by `npx kmwc sync` — repo targets in Makefile.local
└── Dockerfile, nginx.conf    # GENERATED — examples image (make image-build / image-run, port 12610)
```

The examples site and the e2e server run on the devkit (`@keenmate/web-components-devkit`,
`package.json#kmwc`): `npm run dev` → http://localhost:12600. The package builds itself
(`npm run build` → packages/web-grid: `cem analyze` + tsc + vite library build) and ships
`custom-elements.json` / `web-types.json` / the VS Code data (core `blissAnalyzerConfig()`).

## Development Commands

- `make setup` - Install all workspace dependencies
- `make dev` - Examples dev server with HMR (http://localhost:12600)
- `make build` - Build the library package (incl. the Custom Elements Manifest)
- `make build-examples` - Build the static examples site (dist-examples/)
- `make package` - Build + copy README / ai into the package + npm pack
- `make publish-rc` / `make publish` - Release gates (check-release, e2e) + publish (Makefile.local)
- `npx kmwc doctor` - Devkit + rulebook checks

## Technical Notes

### Scroll Container Setup

The grid supports both horizontal and vertical scrolling. Key CSS pattern:

```css
/* Host element (set by consumer) */
<web-grid style="max-width: 900px; max-height: 400px; display: block;">

/* Shadow DOM container */
.wg {
  max-height: inherit;  /* Picks up host's max-height */
  overflow: auto;       /* Single scroll container for both axes */
}

/* Table */
.wg__table {
  width: max-content;   /* Expand beyond container if columns are wide */
  min-width: 100%;      /* Fill container if columns are narrow */
  table-layout: fixed;  /* Respect explicit column widths */
}
```

**Why `max-height: inherit`?**
- `height: 100%` doesn't work when parent only has `max-height` (no explicit height)
- `max-height: inherit` passes the constraint from host into shadow DOM
- This enables vertical scrolling when content exceeds the max-height

**Why single scroll container?**
- Having separate scroll containers (host for vertical, .wg for horizontal) causes the horizontal scrollbar to only appear when you scroll to the bottom
- Single `.wg` container with `overflow: auto` shows both scrollbars at correct positions

### Sticky Headers

Headers remain visible at the top when scrolling vertically:

```css
.wg__header {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  z-index: 1;  /* Stay above body cells */
  background: var(--wg-header-background);  /* Must be opaque */
}
```

**Why this works:**
- `position: sticky` with `top: 0` pins the element to the top of its scroll container
- The `.wg` container's `overflow: auto` creates the scroll context needed for sticky positioning
- `z-index: 1` ensures headers stay above body cells when scrolling
- Opaque background is essential - otherwise body content shows through the header

**Border placement is critical:**
- The border must be on `.wg` container, NOT on `.wg__table`
- With `border-collapse: collapse`, a table border sits outside/above the header cells
- This creates a gap where content scrolls through when headers stick at `top: 0`
- Moving border to container eliminates the gap

### CSS Variable Architecture: `--base-*` Integration

The `--base-*` CSS variables enable **centralized theming** across all Keenmate components via `@keenmate/theme-designer`.

**Pattern - fallback chain:**
```css
:host {
  /* If --base-primary-color is set on :root by theme-designer, use it */
  /* Otherwise, use hardcoded fallback */
  --wg-accent-color: var(--base-primary-color, #0078d4);
  --wg-font-size-sm: calc(var(--base-font-size-sm, 1.2) * var(--wg-rem));
}
```

**Variables that support `--base-*` fallback:**
- **Typography:** `--base-font-family`, `--base-font-size-*`, `--base-font-weight-*`, `--base-line-height-*`
- **Colors:** `--base-primary-color`, `--base-text-color-*`, `--base-main-bg`, `--base-elevated-bg`, `--base-hover-bg`, `--base-active-bg`, `--base-disabled-bg`, `--base-dropdown-bg`, `--base-border-color`, `--base-input-*`, `--base-danger-*`, `--base-tooltip-*`
- **Other:** `--base-border-radius-*`

**Benefits:**
1. All Keenmate components (web-multiselect, web-daterangepicker, web-grid) share the same base theme
2. Change `:root { --base-primary-color: red }` and all components update
3. Components work standalone with defaults, but integrate with theme-designer when present

### CSS Variable Naming: Component-Specific Variables

When creating new CSS variables, use **component-specific names** that describe their purpose, NOT generic spacing variables directly.

**Wrong - generic variable in styles:**
```css
/* DON'T do this */
.wg__combobox-arrow {
  right: var(--wg-spacing-md);  /* Too generic, unclear purpose */
}
```

**Correct - component-specific variable:**
```css
/* In _variables.css */
:host {
  --wg-dropdown-toggle-right: var(--wg-spacing-md);
}

/* In _base.css */
.wg__combobox-arrow {
  right: var(--wg-dropdown-toggle-right);  /* Clear purpose, easy to adjust */
}
```

**Why this pattern:**
1. **Self-documenting** - variable name explains what it controls
2. **Targeted overrides** - consumers can adjust specific things without affecting others
3. **Consistent with web-multiselect** - see `../web-multiselect/src/css/_variables.css` for reference
4. **Single point of change** - if dropdown toggle needs different spacing, change one variable

**Naming convention:** `--wg-{component}-{property}`
- `--wg-dropdown-toggle-right` - right position of dropdown toggle
- `--wg-toolbar-btn-min-width` - minimum width of toolbar buttons
- `--wg-filter-input-padding` - padding inside filter inputs

### UI Transitions: Keep It Snappy

Prefer **instant state changes** over CSS transitions for UI elements. Snappy feedback feels more responsive.

**Don't add transitions for:**
- Dropdown toggle appearing/disappearing on hover
- Focus/hover state changes
- Cell state changes (editing, focused, etc.)

**Exception:** Pagination buttons have a subtle transition for hover effects, but this is optional.

If in doubt, no transition is better than a slow one.

### Naming Convention: Events vs Callbacks

The grid follows the shared Keenmate interaction model (web-components-core `/actions`, SPEC §12.5 / §12.12). Distinct naming separates notifications from hooks that affect behavior. Every callback takes ONE `ctx` object; every ctx and event detail carries non-enumerable `controller` (`GridController`, also `el.controller`) and `element`.

**Events** - real DOM events (kebab-case, bubble, not composed) + a camelCase `on*` property twin called with the same detail first. Return value is ignored. Declared in the `EVENTS` table in `web-component.ts`, typed in `GridEventMap` (`interaction.ts`):
```typescript
// Grid-level events                    // twin
'row-change'                            // onRowChange       — "row changed" notification
'cell-edit-start' / 'cell-edit-cancel'  // onCellEditStart / onCellEditCancel
'validation-error'                      // onValidationError
'action'                                // onAction          — any toolbar / menu / shortcut item activated
// … focus-change, row-delete, cell-selection-change, row-selection-change,
//   column-selection-change, data-request, filter-change,
//   column-resize, column-reorder, row-expand, row-collapse, expanded-change, row-lock-change, cell-paste

// EditorOptions notification
onSelect(ctx)                           // "option was selected"

// Action items (toolbar / context menu / shortcuts)
onClick(detail)                         // "item was activated" — same detail as the `action` event
```

**Callbacks** - `*Callback` suffix, return value affects component behavior. Prefixes: `get*Callback` (returns a value), `render*Callback` (returns HTML / renders), `create*Callback` (returns a new row), `before*Callback` (`false` cancels; async OK where documented):
```typescript
// Column callbacks
getDisplayValueCallback  // returns display string
renderCellCallback       // returns cell HTML
getTooltipCallback       // returns tooltip text
validateCallback         // returns ValidateResult → marks invalid / transforms
renderEditorCallback     // takes over cell editing (ctx.commit / ctx.cancel)

// Grid callbacks
getRowClassCallback, createEmptyRowCallback, createDuplicateRowCallback,
beforeActionCallback, beforeContextMenuOpenCallback, beforePasteCallback, beforeFillCallback

// EditorOptions callbacks
getDisplayValueCallback  // returns display text for option
searchCallback           // returns search results (async)
renderOptionCallback     // returns HTML string for option
```

Built-in item names are kebab-case (`'move-up'`, `'sort-asc'`, `'expand'`) and the row built-ins (`add`, `delete`, `duplicate`, `move-up`, `move-down`) do the work themselves BEFORE the `action` event (core order: beforeActionCallback → onClick → built-in → `action`); `delete` then fires `row-delete` (after the fact; Ctrl+Delete runs the same built-in). Do not add lowercase `on*` properties (they collide with native `HTMLElement` handlers like `onpaste` / `onselect`).

### v2 naming rules (suite-wide, BlissFramework naming-conventions D-NC-13..27)

- Boolean attributes are the short HTML form derived from the config key: `is*Shown` → `show-*`, `is*Enabled` → `enable-*`, `should*` → bare, `is*Allowed` → `allow-*`, layout / appearance variants and data hints `is<Adj>` → bare (`isStriped` → `striped`). Feature switches are `is*Enabled` (`isFilteringEnabled` / `enable-filtering`, `isPagingEnabled` / `enable-paging`, `isEditingEnabled` / `enable-editing`). `isReadonly` / `isDisabled` → `readonly` / `disabled`.
- Enum values kebab-case; "off" is `'none'`; `multiple`, never `multi`. No bare `mode` (`preset`).
- Events: `<state>-change` for set changes (whole new state: `expanded-change { paths }`, `focus-change`, `*-selection-change`), `<domain>-<verb>` for acts (`row-expand`, `row-delete`, `cell-paste`, `cell-edit-start`). Detail nouns: never a bare `index` (`rowIndex`, `optionIndex`), `old*` / `new*` pairs, `item` only for the core `ActionItem`.
- State is a same-named property on the element AND `el.controller` (controller read-only): `selectedRows` (objects), `selectedRowIndices`, `items`, `displayItems`, `columns`, `sort`, `filters`, `invalidCells`, `selectedCellRange`, `expandedPaths`. `get*()` only for lookups with arguments / computed snapshots (`getDrafts`, `getSelectedCells`, `getSelectedColumns`).
- Verbs: remove = programmatic (`removeRows`, `removeRow`), delete = user command (`delete` built-in + `row-delete`), clear = empty a set (`clearSelection` = all kinds), discard = drafts (`discardDraft(row)`), open/close = surfaces you work in (`openGoToRowDialog`), `scrollTo*` → `Promise<boolean>`.
- UI strings only through `labels` (`labels.ts`: `resolveLabels` / `formatLabel`); empty-table keys `noData` (no rows) / `noResults` (filter matched nothing); `''` = blank, `undefined` = default. No `*Text` options.
- Lifecycle from core: `defer` / `release()` / `ready` / `whenReady()` / `destroy()`; engine setters don't render before the first build (`#isBuilt`).

**Why this matters:**
- Events can be safely ignored - component works without them
- Callbacks affect behavior - component depends on return value
- Clear naming prevents confusion about whether return value matters
